commit_message:
riscv: Provide a vector only implementation of Chacha20 cipher

Although we have a Zvkb version of Chacha20, the Zvkb from the RISC-V
Vector Cryptography Bit-manipulation extension was ratified in late 2023
and does not come to the RVA23 Profile. Many CPUs in 2024 currently do not
support Zvkb but may have Vector and Bit-manipulation, which are already in
the RVA22 Profile. This commit provides a vector-only implementation that
replaced the vror with vsll+vsrl+vor and can provide enough speed for
Chacha20 for new CPUs this year.

Signed-off-by: Yangyu Chen <cyy@cyyself.name>

Reviewed-by: Paul Dale <ppzgs1@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/24069)

fix_commit.message: Fix riscv64 chacha crash due to unaligned data
fix_commit.author: Bernd Edlinger

findings.title: Missing pointer-alignment check before dispatching to RISC-V vector ChaCha20 routines
findings.message: ChaCha20_ctr32() on riscv64 selects the vector/Zbb (and optionally Zvkb) assembly implementations of ChaCha20 purely based on length and CPU feature flags (RISCV_HAS_ZBB(), riscv_vlen() >= 128, RISCV_HAS_ZVKB()). It never checks whether the `out` and `inp` buffer pointers are aligned to the machine word size. The RISC-V vector assembly routines (ChaCha20_ctr32_v_zbb / ChaCha20_ctr32_v_zbb_zvkb) use vector load/store instructions that, on real hardware with the Vector (V) extension enabled, can fault or crash on unaligned pointers even though it works fine under QEMU emulation. Since callers of ChaCha20_ctr32() (e.g. EVP cipher code) do not guarantee any particular alignment of input/output buffers, this leads to a crash (SIGBUS/SIGSEGV/illegal instruction depending on platform) whenever a caller passes unaligned buffers on real riscv64 V-extension hardware, i.e. a denial-of-service by user-controlled buffer alignment.
findings.suggestion: Add an alignment check for both the `out` and `inp` pointers to the dispatch condition, falling back to the portable C implementation (ChaCha20_ctr32_c) whenever either buffer is not aligned to sizeof(size_t), as done in the upstream fix.

ground_truth.root_cause: The feature-detection-based dispatch logic for selecting the RISC-V vector ChaCha20 implementation checked only CPU capability flags (RISCV_HAS_ZBB, riscv_vlen, RISCV_HAS_ZVKB) and input length, but never validated pointer alignment of the `out`/`inp` buffers before invoking vector load/store based assembly routines that require (or strongly prefer) aligned accesses on real hardware.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Missing pointer-alignment check before dispatching to RISC-V vector ChaCha20 routines
